record.paper_title: Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities and the Numerical approximation of singular integrals for exponential weights: Methods, Results and Open Problems, Some new, some old.
record.original_question: Let I=(c,d) with -infinity <= c < 0 < d <= infinity. Let w:I -> (0,infinity) be an admissible exponential weight in the following sense: Q=log(1/w) is continuously differentiable and Q(0)=0; Q' is nondecreasing on I and Q(x) tends to infinity as x approaches c from the right and d from the left; T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x), for x != 0, is quasi-increasing on (0,d), quasi-decreasing on (c,0), and satisfies T(x) >= lambda > 1; for some epsilon_0 in (0,1), T(y) is comparable to T(y(1 - epsilon_0/T(y))) for y != 0; and for every epsilon > 0 there is delta > 0 such that the local integral of |Q'(s)-Q'(x)|/|s-x|^(3/2) over x +/- delta x/T(x) is at most epsilon |Q'(x)| sqrt(T(x)/|x|). Given a triangular array chi_n={x_{1,n},...,x_{n,n}}, Cotes numbers lambda_{j,n}, a smooth factor V that decays near the endpoints c and d, p>0, and algebraic polynomials P of degree at most n-1, can one establish forward and converse Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund quadrature estimates of the forms sum_j lambda_{j,n} w(x_{j,n})^(-2) V(x_{j,n}) |P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p <= C integral_I |P(x)w(x)|^p V(x) dx and ||P w||_p <= C (sum_j lambda_{j,n} w(x_{j,n})^(-2) |P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p)^(1/p), establish corresponding polynomial density criteria such as endpoint decay of f w/V, and use these tools to prove mean and uniform convergence of Lagrange interpolation and orthogonal expansions, including rates of convergence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I=(c,d)$ with $-\infty\le c<0<d\le\infty$, and let $w:I\to(0,\infty)$ be an admissible exponential weight in the following sense. Write $Q=\log(1/w)$ and assume:

(i) $Q$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with $Q(0)=0$;
(ii) $Q'$ is nondecreasing on $I$, and $Q(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to c^+$ and as $x\to d^-$;
(iii) the function $T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x)$ ($x\ne0$) is quasi-increasing on $(0,d)$ and quasi-decreasing on $(c,0)$, and satisfies $T(x)\ge\lambda>1$ for all $x\ne 0$;
(iv) there exists $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1)$ such that $T(y)\sim T\!\left(y\bigl(1-\varepsilon_0/T(y)\bigr)\right)$ for $y\ne 0$;
(v) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that
$$\int_{x-\delta x/T(x)}^{x+\delta x/T(x)}\frac{|Q'(s)-Q'(x)|}{|s-x|^{3/2}}\,ds\;\le\;\varepsilon\,|Q'(x)|\sqrt{T(x)/|x|}\qquad(x\ne 0).$$

For each $n\ge 1$ fix an array $\chi_n=\{x_{1,n},\dots,x_{n,n}\}\subset I$ of distinct interpolation nodes together with positive "Cotes numbers" $\{\lambda_{j,n}\}_{j=1}^n$. Let $V:I\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth weight factor that decays at the endpoints $c$ and $d$, let $0<p<\infty$, and let $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ denote the algebraic polynomials of degree at most $n-1$.

Problem. Determine sufficient (and where possible necessary) conditions on $w$, $V$, $p$, and on the arrays $(\chi_n,\lambda_{j,n})$ under which the following hold uniformly in $n$ and in $P\in\mathcal P_{n-1}$:

(a) Forward Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund quadrature estimate
$$\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,V(x_{j,n})\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p \;\le\; C\int_I |P(x)w(x)|^p\,V(x)\,dx;$$

(b) Converse Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund estimate
$$\|Pw\|_{L^p(I)} \;\le\; C\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p\Bigr)^{1/p}.$$

(c) Establish corresponding polynomial density criteria, in particular characterizing those continuous $f$ for which weighted polynomial approximation $\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\|(f-P)w\|$ tends to $0$, including endpoint-decay conditions on $fw/V$.

(d) Apply the resulting estimates to prove mean ($L^p$) and uniform convergence of Lagrange interpolation operators at the nodes $\chi_n$ and of orthogonal expansions with respect to $w^2$, and to obtain quantitative rates of convergence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a survey on Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund inequalities and numerical approximation of singular integrals for exponential weights. While partial results exist for special subclasses (e.g. Freud and Erdős weights, smooth even exponential weights), a complete theory of forward/converse MZ quadrature inequalities, density criteria, and convergence of Lagrange interpolation and orthogonal expansions at the full level of generality of admissible exponential weights on an arbitrary interval $(c,d)$ has not been established.
